newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday July 25.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said after a meeting with prime minister Romano Prodi that the parliamentary majority supporting the centre-left government was "at risk". Bertinotti said it was necessary to settle the differences in order to keep the majority together (all).

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said in an interview that welfare state reforms were the key to the country's economic recovery and the pensions system ought to be reformed as soon as possible (La Stampa).

* Energy group ENI said it was taking a 35 percent stake in Albacom, a telecoms venture owned by British Telecom, Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and communications group Mediaset. ENI also said it would underwrite a 173 billion lire capital increase in Albacom (all).

* Electricity utility ENEL said it would stop buying excess power supply from independent producers and municipal companies. The energy sector watchdog said it intended to examine ENEL's decision (all).

* Stock market watchdog Consob said shares in Italian bank Credito Bergamasco were suspended from Milan bourse for Thursday pending the release of a statement on the bank's future. French banking group Credit Lyonnais is expected to sell its 56.8 percent stake in Credem to Banca Popolare di Verona (all).

* A spokesman for the Milan stock exchange council said shares in newly enlisted Aereoporti di di Roma were temporarily suspended after they were quoted 31 percent higher than their offer price in pre-trading. Aereoporti di Roma bought a 15 percent stake in Aereoporti di Genova (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Shares in retail distribution group Standa were suspended on Thursday and Friday pending the release of a statement (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
